result: In 19 women with CFS vs 20 sedentary controls, cognition did not differ before treadmill exercise to exhaustion, but CFS scored lower immediately after and 24 h after on SDMT (64 vs 69 at 24 h), Stroop word (134 vs 148) and Stroop colour (101 vs 106).
reason: Measures post-exercise cognitive performance, not PEM onset, duration or recovery time; fits neuro-cognition (worse after exertion).

result: In 19 women with CFS vs 20 sedentary controls, cognition did not differ before treadmill exercise to exhaustion, but CFS scored lower immediately after and 24 h after on SDMT (64 vs 69 at 24 h), Stroop word (134 vs 148) and Stroop colour (101 vs 106).
reason: Same measures of processing speed and attention; adds a post-maximal-exercise deficit that lasts at least 24 h, with no deficit at baseline.

result: In 71 CFS vs 65 sedentary controls, only IgG1 and IgG3 of 18 immune variables differed, both lower in CFS; IgG1 was lowest in CFS with axis-I disorder, and the subclass difference was not significant once the MS (n=23) and depression (n=21) groups were included.
reason: Found lower IgG1/IgG3 vs controls, the same direction as the finding, so not a contradiction; adds that the reduction is not specific to CFS and may be an artefact of group composition.

result: FDG-PET in 18 CFS vs 6 healthy controls showed hypometabolism in right mediofrontal cortex (P=0.010) and brainstem (P=0.013); 6 depressed patients had frontal hypometabolism but normal brainstem metabolism.
reason: Independent brainstem imaging abnormality; adds a glucose-metabolism modality and a depression comparison, but the control group is tiny.

result: In 16 adolescents with CFS vs 26 syncope patients and 13 controls, all time- and frequency-domain HRV indices (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, HF, LF, total power) were markedly lower at rest and during 80-degree tilt, with no sympathetic shift on tilt.
reason: Independent paediatric cohort with the same measure (reduced HRV including HF power), same direction.

result: 13 of 16 adolescents with CFS developed neurally mediated hypotension/syncope on 80-degree tilt (5 pure vasodepressor), and their HRV indices were markedly depressed.
reason: Reports neurally mediated hypotension/syncope, not HR-defined POTS; no atlas finding on NMH prevalence, and the HRV result is covered by the neuro-hrv link.

result: Echocardiography in 273 CFS vs 72 controls showed smaller LV end-systolic (p<0.001) and end-diastolic (p=0.008) dimensions, thinner posterior walls, lower LV mass (p=0.006) and smaller carotid diameters.
reason: Large independent cohort, smaller LV dimensions at rest, same direction; the authors attribute it to deconditioning and did not measure blood volume.

result: Echocardiography in 273 CFS vs 72 controls showed smaller LV dimensions and mass and smaller carotid diameters, which the authors interpreted as physical and cardiovascular deconditioning.
reason: Not a replication: it argues for deconditioning, and only by interpretation, with no matched-fitness, comparison-group or bed-rest design; the cardiac data are covered by the small-heart link.

result: In a family with 8 CFS cases, 51Cr-release NK activity across 68 samples over 2 years was lower in cases than in 8 controls (P=0.006), with persistently low activity in 6/8 cases and 4/12 unaffected relatives; NK cell counts were normal.
reason: Same assay type and direction (reduced NK cytotoxicity with normal counts); very small single-family sample.

result: Describes one family in which 5 of 6 siblings and 3 other relatives developed CFS, with low NK activity in cases and some unaffected relatives.
reason: Single-pedigree case report; does not estimate relative risk, twin concordance or familiality.
